title: Observability platform launch page

outcome.problem: Engineering leaders cannot quickly distinguish the product from generic observability vendors or verify that it fits high-stakes incident response.
outcome.desiredChange: A qualified engineering leader understands the operational advantage, trusts the claims, and requests a technical evaluation.
antiGoals: Use visual spectacle that obscures evidence

audiences.label: VP Engineering or platform lead
audiences.context: Arrives from a peer recommendation or technical article while comparing tools under time pressure.

primary.completionSignal: the evaluation form is submitted with company and stack context

secondary.object: the evidence behind the product claims
secondary.completionSignal: the architecture and incident evidence sections are viewed

values.name: operational clarity
values.expression: Evidence is legible and causal relationships are explicit.

values.name: calm authority
values.expression: Measured language, controlled contrast, and precise technical detail.
values.avoid: Urgency theatre, inflated certainty, or aggressive conversion pressure.

values.name: earned distinctiveness
values.expression: A recognizable evidence-led composition built from product truth.
values.avoid: Generic gradient cards, glowing orbs, and copied category conventions.

experience.density: dense where evidence is useful, spacious where decisions need emphasis
experience.familiarity: conventional navigation and forms with a distinctive evidence-led page structure
experience.motion: purposeful state explanation with a complete reduced-motion alternative
experience.hierarchy: one dominant evaluation action supported by progressively deeper proof

criteria.target: At least 12 percent of qualified sessions

criteria.signal: Qualified visitors who inspect architecture or incident evidence

hard.statement: Meet WCAG 2.2 AA for the tested states and preserve complete keyboard operation.
hard.verification: axe-core, keyboard trace, contrast measurement, and manual review

hard.statement: Every performance or reliability claim must point to approved evidence.
Do not overwrite protected application, infrastructure, or content files.
hard.verification: baseline hash, path allowlist, and diff review

soft.statement: Keep the launch page inside the agreed Core Web Vitals budget.
Express recurring visual decisions as tokens and components.

content.sourceOfTruth: approved launch copy and product evidence repository

risks.statement: Visual confidence could overstate incomplete evidence.
risks.control: Require claim provenance and separate confidence from visual emphasis.

risks.statement: Later AI edits could flatten the direction into generic components.
risks.control: Persist candidate decisions, tokens, protected paths, and baseline reference.

assumptions: Qualified visitors understand common observability concepts.
The product team can provide approved incident evidence before release.
openQuestions: Which proof artifact produces the strongest evaluation intent?
Does the dark state ship at launch or remain an evaluation state?
